purpose: Let a founder weigh Alliance AI Partners fairly against hiring locally, US and Australian agencies and per-seat AI tools, with a source and a date for every number, say honestly when each option is the right choice, and move them to an AI check-up.

seo.title: Compare: hiring locally, agencies and AI tools | Alliance AI Partners
seo.description: What it costs to hire a developer in the US, the UK or Australia, what agencies charge by the hour and what per-seat AI tools cost, compared like for like with Alliance AI Partners. Every figure sourced and dated.

content.heading: Agency rates: where the gap is, and where it isn’t.
content.lead: Clutch, a marketplace of reviewed agencies, publishes the hourly ranges most agencies charge. For web development and design, Philippine agencies charge far less. For AI development, Australian and Philippine agencies sit in the same band.

items.title: Web development [5]
items.text: US and Australia: US$100 to US$149 an hour. Philippines: US$25 to US$49.

items.title: Web design [6]
items.text: US and Australia: US$100 to US$149 an hour. United Kingdom: US$50 to US$99. Philippines: under US$25.

items.title: AI development [7]
items.text: United States: US$50 to US$99 an hour. Australia: US$25 to US$49. Philippines: US$25 to US$49.

body: US dollars an hour, September 2026. These are marketplace ranges, not official statistics, and the Philippine ranges describe typical agencies, not our prices. We don’t bill by the hour: every project gets a fixed quote.

content.heading: What per-seat AI tools cost as you grow.
content.lead: Ready-made AI tools are priced per person or per use. They are quick to start, and the bill rises with every person you add and every busy month.

items.title: US$1,500 [8]
items.text: A month for 50 people on Microsoft 365 Copilot: US$30 per user a month, paid yearly, on top of a Microsoft 365 plan.

items.title: Per outcome [9]
items.text: Intercom’s Fin is US$0.99 per outcome, with seats extra.

items.title: Per call [10]
items.text: Smith.ai’s AI receptionist is US$150 a month for 75 calls, then US$2.50 a call.

items.title: What we do instead
items.text: No per-seat fees on the tools we build. AI usage, like model fees, is passed on at cost and shown on its own invoice line.

content.heading: When each option is the right choice.
content.lead: Each one is right for some work. If we are not the right choice for yours, we will say so.

items.title: Hiring locally
items.text: Right when: the role is permanent and central to your business, and you want that skill on your own payroll, in your own office.
items.meta: Watch for: recruiting time, benefits, equipment and office space, all on top of pay.

items.title: A US or Australian agency
items.text: Right when: the work needs people on site, or in the room with your customers.
items.meta: Watch for: hourly billing. Slow work costs more and the final bill is hard to predict, so ask for a fixed quote.

items.title: A per-seat AI tool
items.text: Right when: a ready-made tool already does the job. Our AI assistant rollout service sets up ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot or Gemini across your company, with the right security settings.
items.meta: Watch for: costs rise with every person you add, so check which seats you need.

items.title: Alliance AI Partners
items.text: Right when: you need AI tools, software or automation built around how your business works, or more developers without hiring, and a team that stays to run it and help you grow.
items.meta: Watch for: our team is in the Philippines, so you won’t meet us in your office. We work inside your team: you see progress every week, and a person reviews every piece of work.

content.heading: How we keep this comparison fair.
content.lead: The rules we follow whenever we compare prices, and how we worked out every cost on this page.

items.title: Like with like
items.text: A full-time employee’s yearly cost against our price for a full-time embedded developer, and an agency’s hourly rate against how we price the same work.

items.title: A source and a date for every number
items.text: We update the US and UK figures every year, when new data comes out.

items.title: Marketplace ranges, marked as such
items.text: Clutch ranges describe typical agencies. They are not official statistics, and they are not our prices.

items.title: No gap where there isn’t one
items.text: For AI development, Australian and Philippine agencies charge in the same band, so we don’t claim a gap with Australia.

items.title: Figures, not superlatives
items.text: We give you the real number and let you decide.

body: United States [1][2]: median pay from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (May 2025). Benefits make up 30.8% of total compensation for professional workers (June 2026), so we divided pay by 0.692.

United Kingdom [3]: median pay for full-time programmers and software development professionals from the ONS (2026 provisional figures), plus employer National Insurance at 15% above £5,000 and the minimum 3% employer pension contribution (2026-27 rates).
Australia [4]: median weekly pay for software and applications programmers from Jobs and Skills Australia (ABS data, May 2025), times 52, plus the 12% superannuation guarantee.
Not included: recruiting fees, equipment and office space, so the real cost of hiring is higher.

notes: Later-phase page. Every figure comes from the Brand DNA cost comparison, the Clutch agency ranges and the per-seat examples, each with a Source key and a dated source line in its own section, plus the full list with links in the fairness section. Rules applied: like for like (employee yearly cost against an embedded developer; agency hourly ranges shown as market ranges, not against our prices); no superlatives; Clutch ranges marked as marketplace ranges that describe typical Philippine agencies, not our prices; no AI development gap claimed with Australia; no 'about half' claim until real prices exist. Our prices stay [PRICE]. Header marks Pricing as the current section. Layouts: text-led hero with an index, table, chart card, navy stat split, split-sticky with an inset image, two-column text, full-bleed band with the text on the right. Ribbon signature once: the Ribbon rule over the hero index.
